title: Wired Hem Anarkali: Why It Flares So Beautifully and How to Care for It
excerpt: A thin wire stitched into the hem gives a chiffon Anarkali its soft, wavy ruffle. What a wired hem is, who it suits, how to style it and how to wash and store it so the wave lasts.
body:
A wired hem is a thin, flexible wire stitched into the bottom edge of a garment. On a light fabric like chiffon, it makes the hem curl into a soft, wavy ruffle that holds its shape instead of falling flat. That is why some Anarkalis seem to float and swirl when you walk.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz Styling Team, Jaipur.*

**Quick answer**

- A wired hem has a thin wire sewn into the edge of the flare
- It gives light fabrics a wavy, lettuce-edge ruffle that keeps its shape
- It works best on chiffon, georgette and organza
- Do not wring, twist or crush the hem
- Dry clean, and store it folded loosely, not squashed

## What does a wired hem do?

Chiffon is beautiful because it is so light, but on its own the hem can hang limp. A wire inside the edge gives it a little structure. The fabric gathers into gentle waves along the wire, so the flare looks fuller and frames your feet when you stand, and ripples when you move. It also looks lovely in photos and videos, especially when you twirl.

## Wired hem vs plain hem vs can-can

| | Wired hem | Plain hem | Can-can layer |
|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | Wire sewn into the edge | Simple folded edge | Stiff net layer under the skirt |
| Look | Soft, wavy ruffle at the edge | Straight, natural fall | Puffed, full skirt |
| Weight | Very light | Lightest | Heavier |
| Best for | Chiffon, georgette, organza Anarkalis | Everyday kurtas | Lehengas and gowns |

## Who does a wired hem suit?

Almost everyone. The ruffle adds movement only at the hem, so it does not add bulk at the waist or hips. If you are petite, a calf- or ankle-length flare with a wired hem keeps the look light. If you are tall, it adds drama at the bottom.

New to bandhani? Read [what bandhani is and how to style it](/blog/what-is-bandhani-how-to-style-a-bandhani-anarkali/).

## How do I style a wired-hem Anarkali?

- **Show the hem.** Choose heels or juttis that sit just under the ruffle, and keep pants fitted so the flare stands out.
- **Keep the dupatta light.** Wrap it around the neck or drape it on one shoulder so it does not cover the flare.
- **For a sangeet or mehndi:** silver or kundan jhumkas, a bindi and soft open hair.
- **For a festive dinner:** small studs, a potli bag and a sleek low bun.

## How do I care for a wired hem?

- Dry clean. Ask the cleaner not to press the hem flat.
- Never wring or twist the garment – this can bend the wire out of shape.
- If the wave flattens a little, gently shape it with your fingers and hang it for a few hours.
- Steam lightly instead of ironing the hem.
- Store it folded loosely in a muslin or cotton cloth, at the top of a pile, not squashed under heavy clothes.
- For travel, roll the skirt gently and pack it on top.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is the wire uncomfortable?**
No. It is thin and sits inside the hem, at the bottom of the flare, away from the skin.

**Will the wire break or poke out?**
With normal wear and gentle care, it stays inside the stitching. Avoid crushing or wringing the hem.

**Can I hand wash a wired-hem Anarkali?**
We recommend dry cleaning, especially when there is embroidery on the garment.

**Can the length be changed if it has a wired hem?**
